analysis:
The only changed hunk is in SSDPrefixCache.swift around lines 1772-1779 (head), which is outside the supplied head_text excerpts (lines 1-1255). The supplied units show the unchanged surrounding code: lifecycle, staging lookup/endAdoption, donation, and sidecars. I could not verify the actual changed code, so my conclusion rests on the patch excerpt only.

The patch refactors evictOldestEntry. It adds an `!isClosed` guard, so a closed cache refuses removal. It delegates victim iteration to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:isClosed:), which is not supplied. The per-victim retireIndexedEntries([url]) call and the URL derivation from the HMAC tag via SSDBlockStore.fileURL(root:tag16Hex:) are preserved.

Security-relevant points to check, relating to T-041 and the TTL/LRU purge mitigations:
- Whether the new helper preserves the old behavior of skipping a valid-but-undeletable victim and trying a newer one.
- Whether it preserves the early return on externalChange (the old code returned 0 when retired.externalChange).
- Whether the isClosed callback is evaluated per victim.
- Whether the helper's use of index.oldestEntries() ordering and bounded iteration is unchanged.
- Whether stats and evictions are counted only when bytes are freed (freed > 0 appears equivalent).

The supplied excerpt does not show whether externalChange handling survives inside SSDOwnedEntryRetirement. Its absence from the call site is a coverage limit, not proof of a regression. Whether disk-budget enforcement still bounds at-rest ciphertext depends on that helper. The closed-cache guard is a tightening: close() deregisters from SSDDiskBudget, and the guard avoids unlinking after close.

The visible code in the units (HMAC tags, salt folding, TTL touch, in-flight dedupe, close drain) shows no new regression. Integration should review the SSDOwnedEntryRetirement implementation and its tests.
